title: Milky Way arching over La Silla
caption: The Milky Way arching over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way arches above ESO's La Silla Observatory in this ultra high definition panorama by ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek. Our galaxy's cloudy, dusty structure forms a brilliant, glowing crown over the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, whose open dome seems to be swallowing the bright smudge of the Large Magellanic Cloud.

In the central and upper parts of the image, clouds and nebulae stand out against the dark sky in pinkish hues, among them the well-known Gum Nebula. Horálek's camera also picked up airglow in several colours, spread across the sky and near the horizon.

La Silla lies at the southern edge of the Atacama Desert, 2400 metres above sea level. From there, its many telescopes take advantage of exceptional atmospheric conditions and one of the darkest night skies on Earth to study the cosmos in fine detail.

understand.summary: This is an ultra high definition ground-based panorama by Petr Horálek; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: Airglow and the pink nebulae are faint, and a camera gathering light over time reveals their colours far more readily than the eye.
